title: Legislative districts of Davao Oriental
wikitext:
{{Short description|Districts of Philippine province}} {{Politics of the Philippines}} The '''legislative districts of Davao Oriental''' are the representations of the [[Provinces of the Philippines|province]] of [[Davao Oriental]] in the [[List of legislatures of the Philippines|various national legislatures]] of the [[Philippines]]. The province is currently represented in the [[House of Representatives of the Philippines|lower house]] of the [[Congress of the Philippines]] through its [[#1st District|first]] and [[#2nd District|second]] congressional districts. == History == {{further|Legislative district of Mindanao and Sulu|Legislative district of Davao}} Prior to gaining separate representation, areas now under the jurisdiction of Davao Oriental were represented under the [[Department of Mindanao and Sulu]] (1917–1935) and the historical [[Davao (province)|Davao Province]] (1935–1967). The enactment of Republic Act No. 4867 on May 8, 1967, split the old Davao Province into [[Davao del Norte]], [[Davao del Sur]] and [[Davao Oriental]].{{cite web|title=Republic Act No. 4867|date=May 8, 1967|website=Chan Robles Law Library|accessdate=November 27, 2017|author=Congress of the Philippines|url=http://laws.chanrobles.com/republicacts/49_republicacts.php?id=4871}} Per Section 4 of R.A. 4867, the incumbent Davao Province representative was to indicate which of the three new provinces he wished to continue to represent; Rep. Lorenzo Sarmiento chose [[Legislative districts of Davao del Norte#Lone District (defunct)|Davao del Norte]], which left the seats for [[Legislative district of Davao del Sur#1968–1972|Davao del Sur]] (together grouped with the chartered city of [[Davao City|Davao]]) and [[#Lone District (defunct)|Davao Oriental]] open for the [[List of special elections to the Philippine Congress#House of Representatives|special elections]] scheduled for November 14, 1967. Davao Oriental comprised [[#Lone District (defunct)|a single congressional district]] from the second half of the [[6th Congress of the Philippines|6th Congress]] until the end of the [[7th Congress of the Philippines|7th Congress]]. Davao Oriental was represented in the [[Interim Batasang Pambansa]] as part of [[Interim Batasang Pambansa#Regional Representatives|Region XI]] from 1978 to 1984, and returned [[#At-Large (defunct)|one representative, elected at large]], to the [[Regular Batasang Pambansa]] in [[1984 Philippine parliamentary election|1984]]. Under the new Constitution which was proclaimed on February 11, 1987, the province was reapportioned into two congressional districts;{{cite web|title=1987 Constitution of the Philippines - Apportionment Ordinance|website=Official Gazette of the Republic of the Philippines|url=http://www.officialgazette.gov.ph/constitutions/the-1987-constitution-of-the-republic-of-the-philippines/the-1987-constitution-of-the-republic-of-the-philippines-ordinance/|author=1986 Constitutional Commission|date=February 2, 1987|accessdate=November 19, 2017}} each elected its member to the restored [[House of Representatives of the Philippines|House of Representatives]] starting [[1987 Philippine legislative election|that same year]]. == 1st District == *'''[[Municipalities of the Philippines|Municipalities]]''': [[Baganga, Davao Oriental|Baganga]], [[Boston, Davao Oriental|Boston]], [[Caraga, Davao Oriental|Caraga]], [[Cateel, Davao Oriental|Cateel]], [[Manay, Davao Oriental|Manay]], [[Tarragona, Davao Oriental|Tarragona]] *'''Population (2020)''': 223,811{{cite web|url=https://psa.gov.ph/sites/default/files/attachments/ird/specialrelease/2_Table%201%20Population%20of%20Legislative%20Districts%20by%20Province%20and%20Selected%20HUC_Component%20City%20Web%20Final-signed.pdf|website=Philippine Statistics Authority|date= 29 October 2021|title=Population of Legislative Districts by Province and Selected Highly Urbanized/Component City: 2020}} {| class="wikitable" style="text-align:center; width:40%;" |- ! width="40%"| Period !
